body: In-scope implementation decisions for attempt2: evidence from current terminal launch/input code identifies hosted PTY bytes as the supported agents' actual tool-approval input route; legacy ACP permission APIs are not current interactive launch hooks. Protect real PTY input with immutable terminal/generation/exact-byte authorization rather than guessing prompt text or inventing callbacks. Do not inflate this into universal protection of unrelated third-party app dialogs, but stop unexpected setup/UAC/auth prompts and retain any evidenced own-agent route outside PTY as an explicit obligation. Custom launch support stays unchanged. Custom desktop integration needs a declared real instruction/tool adapter: exact file consumer with {instructions}, and explicit supported discovery/launch-local adapter without it; actual fresh/resume consumption and same-conversation tool use must be proven, never inferred from env/file/echo. Unsupported/unconfigured programs cannot be claimed integrated; no silent removal of generic terminal support. Raw-HID guardian is only a prototype candidate, not proved human authority, and no mandatory biometry/hardware compatibility requirement is adopted. Native pilot remains unlaunched pending corrected bounded cleanup/private runtime state and fresh explicit permission.
